Universal reactive response against ordinary effect plays. Available in 3 copies, it establishes the fundamental counter threat that shapes all sequencing, held in check by the 4-point PR scoring sacrifice.
Primary tempo engine in the game: grants +2 Mini-Turns (net +1 action) and draws 2 cards. Available in 60.1–77.3% of opening hands; policy over-activation inflates perceived dominance.
In written rules, grants zero-cost PR points while attacking opponent hand size without spending a Mini-Turn. Extremely efficient positive-sum play; completely fail-closed in Engine 4.2.6.

Instant counter possessing ⭐A authority that also draws 1 card from bottom of Graveyard even if countered. Readily accessible in red-heavy hands, over-activated by heuristic AI (97 executions in corpus).

Absolute counter authority capable of shutting down Ultras, Board Lock, and Sudden Death. Extremely powerful but heavily taxed by committing two Aces (8 forgone PR points) and blocked by Two-Queen Defense.

Zero Mini-Turn tactical removal at Instant response speed, completely ignoring rank and suit requirements. Exceptional tempo weapon that punishes unguarded high-value PR cards (88.9% conversion in telemetry).
Written as allowing 10♦ + Two to mimic ⭐A counter authority at Instant speed. Absent from executable Core authority.
Instant counter targeting single-card Anchor plays (Queens, Kings, Ace Anchors). Keeps opponent anchor engines in check, balanced by sacrificing 8 PR points.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: 10 Pts + Entry Aegis (+Bonus Score if 0 Pts)
snowballRanking.reason: Scores 10 points with immediate Aegis; if starting at 0 points, allows scoring a bonus card for free. Enables rare Turn-1 21-point wins with Black Joker; counterplay is currently narrowed by IMPL-12.
Alternative branch of 2B+2R granting +2 Mini-Turns and recovering 1 key card from Exile. Highly situational compared to the Draw 2 branch.
The sole designated counter to Scuttle attempts. Preserves high-value PR cards and creates latent defensive threat merely by sitting in hand.
Commits 2 Jacks to gain +2 Mini-Turns (net +1 action). Clean action accelerator, though requiring a true pair of Jacks.
Publicly visible threat deterrence that converts a sacrificed Ace into a stolen opponent card (revealed until Start). Consumes an Action Mini-Turn upfront, trading tempo for future card advantage.
Instant-speed point denial that reduces an enemy PR card's contribution to 0 until that player scores again. Highly effective for denying lethal victory at End Phase.
Converts 10♦ and a Two into +2 Mini-Turns (net +1 action). Inferior to 10♥ which does this as a single card and draws 1.
Written as a 7-point net goal swing (+5 to opponent, -2 to self). Major strategic lever, but unenumerated in Core.
Deploys into ER providing 9 anchor points. Highest single anchor value in the game, but sacrifices K♠'s multi-play counter and Wild Sovereignty.
Deploys into ER providing 7 anchor points (61 executions in corpus). Decisive for winning Exhausted tiebreakers while keeping PR safe from Scuttle.
Exceptional card sculpting tool that discards 1–2 cards, draws 6, and keeps 3–4. Gives 6♠ tremendous mid-to-late game value for assembling lethal lines.
Destroys any enemy PR card, bypassing ordinary Scuttle immunity (e.g. against Aces, Fives, Red Joker). Stopped by Aegis and carries a massive 16-point opportunity cost.
Zero net card cost: draws 1 card immediately while preventing the active player from repeating their chosen Action type this turn. Exceptional tactical limiter (160 executions in corpus).
Destroys any enemy PR card ignoring Scuttle immunity by combining 10♦ and a Two. Heavy 12-point commitment.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: Attach to Enemy Anchor, Gain Control
snowballRanking.reason: Steals an enemy ER Anchor (including Queens and Kings). Stealing a Queen transfers her Guard to the caster, flipping board protection upside down.
Written as raising opponent's Goal by 5 at the cost of discarding an additional card. Unenumerated in Core.
Massive hand sculpting tool that lets 2♠ dig 6 cards deep into the deck. Exceptional for assembling combo pieces or lethal scoring lines late in the game.
In written design, scoring a Seven grants 7 PR points AND reveals 2 cards to take 1 into hand. Massive card-plus-point value; completely blocked in Engine 4.2.6 by IMPL-01.
Written as a Quick reorder of top 4 DP cards and drawing 1 without spending a Mini-Turn. Excellent deck manipulation, but unimplemented in executable Core.
Enters ER as an anchor, reveals opponent's complete hand, and forces 1 discard. Only 1 active Nine Anchor allowed at a time.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: Steal OTT Card, Tap to Start
snowballRanking.reason: Steals any enemy OTT card, bypassing Guard and rank immunity. Hold mode taps it until Start, allowing the caster to deploy its effect for free or keep it as an anchor.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: Attach to Enemy PR Card (+1, Control)
snowballRanking.reason: Seizes control of an enemy PR card and adds +1 point to it. Creates substantial 2-way point swings (e.g. stealing a 10 swings 21 points), but vulnerable to Jack severance.
Forces opponent to discard hand and redraw size - 2. Severe resource stripping against opponents holding large hands.
Discards hand and draws new hand containing discarded count + 3. Superb hand refresh when holding dead cards.
Written as permanently raising opponent's Goal by 3 at Instant speed. Unenumerated in Core authority.
Written as drawing 1 from top/bottom of Graveyard when resolving an ordinary Scuttle using an Eight. Unimplemented in engine.
Draws 3 cards, keeps 2, and returns 1 to top/bottom of DP. Net +1 card and clean selection, competing against a strong 6-point PR score.
Written as inspecting face-down Swap Bar cards and taking or immediately casting one without spending a Mini-Turn. Unimplemented in Core engine.
Written as an Instant-speed bounce to top or bottom of DP. Highly potent reactive disruption, but absent from executable Core authority.
Draws 3 and discards 1 from hand to GY. Fuels Graveyard strategies while netting +1 card in hand.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: Steal OTT Card, Score to PR
snowballRanking.reason: Immediately transfers an enemy card into the caster's PR as points. Generally inferior to Hold mode in practice, because Hold allows scoring at next Start while preserving effect options. However, Score mode provides immediate, undisruptable PR points — the tapped card in Hold mode can be answered by K♠ or other removal before Start.
Enables K♠ to sculpt the hand 6 cards deep, exiling K♠. High-commitment digging tool when searching for game-winning lines.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: Shuffle DP + GY into DP, Draw 2
snowballRanking.reason: Shuffles Graveyard back into Draw Pile and draws 2 cards. Refills exhausted deck and recycles all spent power cards.
Written as forcing presentation of 2 cards and immediately scoring or casting one under your control. High ceiling, but fail-closed in Engine 4.2.6.
Mills 2 cards, rummages 1 from Graveyard into hand, and draws the bottom Graveyard card. Generates net +1 card advantage while recycling spent resources.
Card advantage engine yielding net +1 card for a 2-point sacrifice. Solid mid-game value play when the Graveyard is populated.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: Draw GY Bottom or Refine Hand
snowballRanking.reason: Free Start-phase trigger allowing the player to draw the bottom Graveyard card or discard 1 and draw 1. High utility resource smoothing.
Completely swaps hands with an opponent. Devastating when caster has an empty or depleted hand and opponent has hoarded high-value cards.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: Take Top DP to Hand or PR
snowballRanking.reason: Free Start-phase trigger allowing the player to add the top DP card to hand or score it directly. Zero card commitment once the threshold is met.
Mills 4 and draws 2 from bottom of GY. High resource cost (2 Fives = 10 PR points sacrificed) for modest card advantage.
Tri-modal composite action: scores 1 card, resolves 1 card's effect internally (uncounterable sub-cast), and exiles 1 card. High flexibility, but consumes 3 dedicated black cards.
Written as allowing chained Topdeck Casting when a physical Seven is revealed. Recursion helper is dead code in the engine.
Written as an alternate win condition: scraps an enemy card and begins an inexorable 2-turn victory countdown. Extremely rare (<0.1% reachability), unrepresented in executable play.
Forces opponent to present cards and steals up to 2 (revealed until Start). Direct hand disruption that simultaneously expands the caster's hand.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: When Scored: Move <=2 Exile to DP
snowballRanking.reason: Written as recycling up to 2 cards from Exile back into DP when Black Joker is scored. Blocked in Engine 4.2.6 by IMPL-01 scoring refusal.
Commits two Threes to strip a card directly from the opponent's hand. High card investment for a single hand steal, limited to Unrestricted profile.
Written as revealing 3 cards from DP for greater assignment choice. Unimplemented in executable engine.
Written as mimicking ⭐5 Super Recycle. Unimplemented in Core.
Reveals top 2 DP cards: 1 added to hand (revealed), 1 declared immediately as a generated play. Value is heavily distorted in executable game by missing 7-point scoring fallback.
Written as mimicking ⭐3 Super Raid with 10♦ + Two. Unimplemented in Core.
Forces opponent to discard up to 2 cards of their choice. Pure card attrition, useful against opponents hoarding combos or responses.
Gambit play that reveals 2 cards from DP, adding one to hand and generating an immediate play. High variance, but cheaper than playing a Seven.
Written as mimicking ⭐6 Super Dig. Unimplemented in Core.
Free Start-phase guess: if both rank and suit match the top DP card, scores it immediately. Low probability of success (~1.9%) without deck inspection.
Copies 5-Recycle, permanently exiling K♠ for net +1 card advantage. Generally inferior to holding K♠ for counterplay.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: Bounce OTT Card to Top DP
snowballRanking.reason: Removes an exposed enemy card to the top of the Draw Pile. Disrupts tempo, but gives the opponent the card back on their next draw.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: Bounce OTT Card to Top DP
snowballRanking.reason: Copies rank-3 bounce for only 2 points forgone rather than 3. Decent tempo tool against exposed enemy cards, though subject to standard Guard and Ace counterplay.
The ultimate board reset: clears every card from PR and ER across all players, hard-bypassing Guard, Aegis, Q♠, and all immunities. Wipes own board too, enforcing fair comeback symmetry.
Provides a single-card global board reset for only 2 points forgone and zero extra discard cost. Highest efficiency board wipe in the game, turning 2♠ into a second natural 4♠.
Written as accessing any card in Exile without positional restrictions. Most flexible written Exile rummage; fail-closed in Engine 4.2.6.
Executes 4♠ Total Clear via K♠ at the steep cost of discarding an additional card and exiling K♠ permanently. Crucial third access route to Total Clear.
Single-card Row Exchange executed through 10♦ without needing a second Four. Inverts points boards while granting Aegis, currently protected from Base Ace by IMPL-12.
The sole targeted single-card Exile recovery in the game. Swaps 10♠ for any exiled card (revealed until Start), exiling 10♠ in the process.
Wipes all vulnerable enemy PR cards to the Graveyard for 1 Action. Major comeback equalizer that prevents opponents from running away with point leads, stopped cleanly by Aegis.
Gambit play that exiles K♠ to cast from top of deck. Rarely justified given K♠'s defensive counter value.
Specific targeted answer that explicitly pierces Aegis immunity. Highly valuable in Aegis-heavy boards (e.g. against 8-Quick or ⭐4), but narrow when no Aegis is active.
Written as rummaging from the newest 2 cards in Exile. Entirely unimplemented in code, collapsing into generic 5 Recycle.
Wipes all enemy ER Anchors (except Q♠ and Aegised cards) to the Graveyard. Essential tool for breaking Queen Guard fortresses and King anchor totals.
Structurally swaps PR rows between players and grants Aegis to all exchanged cards. Can produce a massive instant 20+ point swing when trailing, but requires 2 Fours and is countered by K♠.
Written as mimicking ⭐7 Sequential Topdeck. Unimplemented in Core.
Written as rummaging from the oldest 2 cards in Exile. Unimplemented in engine.
Swaps Enduring Rows, seizing an opponent's entire anchor fortress and granting them Aegis. High setup requirement and niche application compared to PR exchange.

snowballRanking.primitiveName: Bounce OTT Card to Top DP
snowballRanking.reason: Copies 3-Bounce through Wild Sovereignty, exiling K♠ permanently. Poor trade of a premium 8-point counter for a minor bounce.
Single-card Enduring Row swap executed via 10♦, stealing an enemy anchor setup.
Enables any Two to wipe an enemy row for only 2 points sacrificed. Excellent efficiency and comeback potential, respecting Aegis and effect immunities.
Fallback mode when no Aegis exists, bouncing an enemy Anchor to hand. Conditional on zero Aegis existing OTT, limiting its tactical flexibility.
Cross-card inferior to Solo Mimic ⭐4 because it consumes 10♦ PLUS an extra Two for the exact same result. The additional Two card commitment yields zero additional effect.
Written as rummaging from middle Exile cards when Exile has ≥5 cards. Restrictive condition; unimplemented in executable engine.
Designed as an 8-card draw engine. Defect-contaminated in Unrestricted (enumerator forces keep list empty, resulting in pure card loss).
Wipes an enemy row using K♠, exiling K♠ afterward. Useful emergency reset when no Four is held.
Designed as sequential independent Topdeck casting across multiple revealed cards. Defect-contaminated in Unrestricted (empty assignment lists).

strictDominanceFindings.reason: Hold mode seizes the card tapped until Start, retaining the option to score it OR cast its effect for free. Score mode immediately scores it into PR. Hold mode's optionality is usually superior, but Score mode provides immediate, undisruptable PR points — the tapped card in Hold mode can be answered by K♠, Aegis re-activation, or other removal before Start. Hold is the stronger default but does not strictly dominate Score in all states.

strictDominanceFindings.status: CROSS-CARD SUPERIOR (same primitive, lower input cost)
strictDominanceFindings.reason: Solo Mimic achieves the identical Row Exchange effect using only 10♦. Paired Mimic requires 10♦ PLUS an extra Two card. Both routes share the 10♦ component, but Paired Mimic pays an additional card for zero additional effect. This is cross-card route superiority rather than strict dominance because the source card sets differ.

A♠ has identical timing (Instant), identical card cost (1 card), and identical points forgone (4 pts), but adds source-exile (denying Graveyard recursion) and immunity to Base Ace counter-counters. A♠ is functionally superior to Base Ace in reactive trades, balanced only by 1-copy rarity. Cross-card superiority rather than strict dominance because the source cards are different identities.

Both routes execute Total Clear, but 2♠ costs 2 points forgone with zero extra discard and goes to Graveyard, while K♠ costs 8 points forgone, requires an additional discard, and exiles K♠ permanently. 2♠ is vastly more efficient. Cross-card superiority because the source cards are different identities with different opportunity costs.
Sudden Death in Unrestricted consumes a Mini-Turn and never advances, achieving zero game effect. Any functional action strictly dominates this defect.
